result:
On load, the app asks the API who is signed in before rendering anything. `src/app/provider.tsx` wraps the whole tree in `AuthLoader` from `src/lib/auth.tsx`, which is built by `configureAuth` from `react-query-auth`. Its `userFn` is `getUser`, which calls `GET /auth/me` through the Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`. That instance sends cookies (`withCredentials`), so the session cookie goes along. While the request is pending, a spinner shows. The result is cached in React Query, and any component reads it with `useUser()`. `ProtectedRoute` in `src/lib/auth.tsx` wraps the `/app` routes in `src/app/router.tsx` and sends the user to `/auth/login` when `user.data` is empty. `AuthLayout` in `src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx` does the opposite on the login and register pages: once a user is loaded, it navigates to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

When any request fails, the response interceptor in `src/lib/api-client.ts` runs. It first shows an error toast with the server's message, or the Axios error message if the server sent none. If the status is 401, it builds a `redirectTo` value and sends the browser to the login page with `window.location.href`. The request promise is then rejected, so the caller still sees the error. Three things in this code are worth knowing:

- The `redirectTo` lookup is broken. It reads from `new URLSearchParams()`, which is always empty, so it always falls back to `window.location.pathname`. Any query string on the page is lost on the way to sign-in.
- The 401 handler also fires for the `/auth/me` call on load. A signed-out visitor to `/app/...` therefore gets an error toast and a full-page redirect, and `ProtectedRoute` also redirects. Both happen, and I did not run the app to see which one wins.
- The full-page `window.location.href` assignment goes against the project rule that navigation goes through React Router. It also forces a reload, which discards the React Query cache.

The mock API differs from production here. In `src/testing/mocks/handlers/auth.ts`, the `/auth/me` handler returns 500 on any error, not 401, so in development a signed-out user never hits the 401 branch and is redirected only by `ProtectedRoute`. This is from reading the code, not from running it. I made no file changes.
